title: Outlook mobile: Purview DLP wait-on-send for iOS and Android
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and the Microsoft documentation checked. It correctly distinguishes the documented Windows controls from the planned mobile capability, and leaves mobile licensing, defaults and timeout behaviour unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Purview DLP wait-on-send support for Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies.

claims.claim: The planned capability lets organisations require DLP evaluation before an email is sent.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent

claims.claim: Organisations will be able to configure how long users must wait for evaluation.
claims.quote: configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn says Outlook for Android and iOS does not yet support DLP Wait-to-Send.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support DLP Wait‑to‑Send

claims.claim: The mobile policy-tip reference directs readers to the Microsoft 365 Roadmap for future announcements.
claims.quote: For future announcements, see the Microsoft 365 Roadmap

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the planned mobile wait-on-send behaviour in detail.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Opened the mobile policy-tip reference, new Outlook reference and Set-OrganizationConfig; found no mobile implementation details.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for the Exchange organisation wait-on-send parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled admin center UI configuration new Outlook wait to send. Opened the new Outlook policy-tip reference and Set-OrganizationConfig; the former says the experience is controlled solely through the Exchange parameters.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> configures the documented organisation-level Windows wait-on-send settings.
claims.quote:
The DLPWaitOnSendEnabled specifies whether mail sent from Outlook for Windows is evaluated by data loss prevention (DLP). Valid values are:

- $true: Mail sent from Outlook for Windows to Exchange is evaluated by DLP.

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled defaults to false for new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled boolean: true or false. Default: false

claims.claim: The new Outlook policy-tip page gives a timeout range of 0 to 10,000 seconds.
claims.quote: DLPWaitOnSendTimeout Integer: range 0–10,000 seconds.

claims.claim: The documented default for DLPWaitOnSendTimeout is 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999. The default value is 9999.

claims.claim: The Set-OrganizationConfig reference instead gives the valid timeout range as 0 to 9999 seconds.
claims.quote: The DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter specifies how long in seconds Outlook for Windows waits for data loss prevention (DLP) evaluation to complete on a new message before offering an override. A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999.

claims.claim: For new Outlook, timeout values from 1 to 9998 permit sending without completed DLP evaluation after that wait.
claims.quote: A value from 1 to 9998 means Outlook waits for the specified number of seconds before it allows the user to override and send the message without completing DLP evaluation.

claims.claim: A timeout of 0 shows Send Anyway immediately in new Outlook.
claims.quote: The value 0 means the user immeidately sees "Send Anyway" in the infobar of messages they're creating.

claims.claim: A timeout of 9999 prevents sending until DLP evaluation completes in new Outlook.
claims.quote: The value 9999 means the user can't send the message unless the DLP evaluation is complete.

claims.claim: The new Outlook reference says its wait-to-send experience is controlled solely through the two Exchange parameters.
claims.quote: The wait‑to‑send experience is controlled solely through the following Exchange mailbox parameters:

claims.claim: Running the Exchange parameters requires assigned permissions, and Learn directs administrators to find permissions for each cmdlet or parameter.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can run this cmdlet. Although this article lists all parameters for the cmdlet, you might not have access to some parameters if they aren't included in the permissions assigned to you.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the planned mobile implementation reads the same Exchange parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Opened mobile and new Outlook references and Set-OrganizationConfig; the mobile page links the cmdlet but says mobile wait-to-send is not yet supported.

claims.claim: The mobile DLP policy-tip control is under Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management.
claims.quote:
you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center.

You can access this policy under Customization and Policy Management.

claims.claim: The policy is named Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook.
claims.quote: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook

claims.claim: Learn says the policy-tip policies can target individuals or groups.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.claim: The DLP policy-tip UI is turned off by default for Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for the Apps admin center mobile policy-tip UI switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook" PowerShell Graph Cloud Policy API; Microsoft 365 Apps cloud policy service PowerShell Microsoft Graph API policy configurations automation Outlook Android iOS. Opened mobile reference and Cloud Policy overview.

claims.claim: The policy-tip UI setting is not documented as the mobile wait-on-send switch.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled admin center UI configuration new Outlook wait to send. Opened mobile and new Outlook policy-tip references; the mobile switch is described as showing policy tips, while mobile wait-to-send remains unsupported.

claims.claim: The general oversharing DLP policy configuration starts at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule with Name, Policy, NotifyUser Owner, NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption Dialog and ContentContainsSensitiveInformation configures an oversharing dialog rule.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation

claims.claim: The mobile reference says the oversharing dialog is enabled in a DLP rule.
claims.quote: When you enable this feature in a DLP rule, it displays popups for warning, override, or block actions to end users who are sharing labeled or sensitive emails in Outlook for Android and iOS.

claims.claim: The general oversharing configuration uses a DLP policy scoped to Exchange email.
claims.quote: To enable these pop-ups, first scope your policy to the Exchange location and then select the Show policy tip as a dialog for the user before send option

claims.claim: Compliance administrator is one of the role groups listed for creating and deploying the general oversharing policy.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups

- Compliance administrator

claims.claim: Security administrator is another listed role group for creating and deploying the general oversharing policy.
claims.quote:
The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups

- Compliance administrator
- Compliance data administrator
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admin
- Security administrator

claims.where: controls[2].note; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The oversharing get-started page frames its example as Outlook for Microsoft 365, not as the planned mobile feature.
claims.quote: In Outlook for Microsoft 365, an oversharing pop-up displays a pop-up before a message is sent.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The mobile page qualifies oversharing dialog availability with the necessary licences and configuration.
claims.quote: The oversharing dialog is available in DLP for Outlook for Android and iOS users when used with the necessary licenses and configuration.

claims.claim: The mobile policy-tip reference's licensing section names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Android iOS wait-on-send DLP licensing meter pricing Microsoft Purview. Opened the complete mobile policy-tip reference; its Licensing requirements heading has no content before the next section.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The oversharing get-started page states that oversharing pop-ups require a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.
claims.quote: Oversharing pop-ups require a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription, along with a version of Outlook that supports oversharing pop-ups.

claims.claim: The oversharing get-started page also requires a version of Outlook that supports oversharing pop-ups.
claims.quote: along with a version of Outlook that supports oversharing pop-ups.

claims.quote:
For advanced DLP policy tip support, which makes additional DLP conditions, advanced classifiers, oversharing dialog, and more available, these licenses are required for each scoped user:

claims.claim: The same advanced policy-tip licensing list includes Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW.

claims.claim: The same advanced policy-tip licensing list includes Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A licensing model specifically for the planned mobile wait-on-send capability has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Android iOS wait-on-send DLP licensing meter pricing Microsoft Purview. Opened the mobile reference, oversharing get-started page and Purview service description; found general DLP and desktop policy-tip licences but no planned mobile wait-on-send licensing statement.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter for mobile DLP wait-on-send.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Android iOS wait-on-send DLP licensing meter pricing Microsoft Purview. Opened the mobile reference, oversharing get-started page and Purview service description; found no meter for mobile wait-on-send.

claims.claim: The roadmap item does not specify a licence or meter.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies. Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationales
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the new mobile wait-on-send control starts enabled, so its default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read the roadmap description and mobile policy-tip reference; neither states the planned control's default. Existing policy-tip and Windows defaults describe other controls.

claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to the planned mobile wait-on-send feature are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Opened mobile and new Outlook references and oversharing get-started; no planned mobile wait-on-send prerequisites are given.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics for mobile wait-on-send have not been stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read roadmap and mobile reference; the roadmap supplies a month target and the reference points to future announcements, not rollout mechanics.

claims.claim: Mobile wait-on-send release channels have not been stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read roadmap and mobile reference; neither supplies release channels for the mobile feature.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether mobile wait-on-send will offer a Send anyway override.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Opened mobile and new Outlook references; mobile documents existing oversharing overrides but no wait-on-send override behaviour.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how individual timeout values will behave on mobile.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android mobile DLP wait on send licensing prerequisites rollout default DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Opened mobile and new Outlook references and Set-OrganizationConfig; numeric timeout semantics are documented for Windows, not the planned mobile support.

claims.claim: The desktop oversharing page says DLP evaluation duration can vary.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: That desktop page names internet speed as a factor in evaluation duration.
claims.quote: depending on factors such as internet speed

claims.claim: That desktop page names content length as a factor in evaluation duration.
claims.quote: depending on factors such as internet speed, content length

claims.claim: That desktop page names the number of policies as a factor in evaluation duration.
claims.quote: depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no identity or sign-in change.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes waiting for DLP evaluation, not a new autonomous Outlook action.
claims.quote: This helps ensure sensitive information is inspected against organizational policies before messages leave the organization while providing administrators with flexible control over the user experience.
